body.statement:
There exist constants \(c,c'>0\) such that, for any \(c_1,c_2,c_3>0\) satisfying \(cc_1c_3/c_2^2\le 1\) and \(d\le c_3n\log n\), there are two probability distributions \(\nu_0,\nu_1\) on triples \((p,\pi,\mu)\) with the following properties.  Almost surely under either distribution,
\[
 0\le p\le \frac{c_1\log n}{n},\qquad
 \epsilon\le\pi\le1-\epsilon,\qquad 0\le\mu\le1.
\]
Writing \(K=c_2\log n\), for all nonnegative integers \(i,j,k\) with \(i+j+k\le3K\),
\[
 E_{\nu_0}\!\left[p^i(p\pi)^j(p\pi\mu)^k\right]
 =E_{\nu_1}\!\left[p^i(p\pi)^j(p\pi\mu)^k\right].
\]
Moreover,
\[
 a_0:=E_{\nu_0}[p]=E_{\nu_1}[p]\le\frac1d,
 \qquad
 \left|E_{\nu_0}[p\mu]-E_{\nu_1}[p\mu]\right|
 \ge \frac{c_4}{n\log n},
 \qquad c_4=\frac{cc'c_1}{c_2^2}.
\]

source.locator: arXiv:2405.00118v3, Lemma 5 in the proof of Theorem 2, main.tex lines 1539--1560; construction in Appendix D.2, lines 4098--4162
source.verbatim_statement: There exists constants \(c,c'>0\) such that for any constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3>0\) satisfying \(cc_1c_3/c_2^2\leq 1\) and \(d\leq c_3n\log n\), there exist two distributions \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\) on \((p,\pi,\mu)\) satisfying: \(0\leq p\leq c_1\log n/n\), \(\epsilon\leq\pi\leq1-\epsilon\), and \(0\leq\mu\leq1\) almost surely; with \(K=c_2\log n\), \(E_{\mu_0}[p^i(p\pi)^j(p\pi\mu)^k]=E_{\mu_1}[p^i(p\pi)^j(p\pi\mu)^k]\) for nonnegative \(i,j,k\) satisfying \(i+j+k\leq3K\); \(a_0:=E_{\mu_0}[p]=E_{\mu_1}[p]\leq1/d\); and \(|E_{\mu_0}[p\mu]-E_{\mu_1}[p\mu]|\geq c_4/(n\log n)\), where \(c_4=cc'c_1/c_2^2\).

attestation.note: Transcribed directly from the arXiv v3 TeX source, Lemma 5 at main.tex lines 1539--1560, and checked against its construction at lines 4098--4162.

body.justification: These matched triple moments are the published substrate for the rare-cell count-mixture construction.
body.gap: The cited lemma supplies approximate-mass priors, not exact fixed-sample probability-law priors; the consumer theorem proves the confidence-interval de-Poissonization separately.
body.consumer: The rare-cell component of the honest confidence-length converse.
